subject: Private deployment: ops playbook & SLA gap clarification
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@halcyon-tx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@halcyon-tx.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed latency spikes in private VPC — need attribution

Hi Karthik,

We spotted repeated latency spikes for inference calls to the private deployment that was commissioned last quarter. The spikes appear to align with certain batch jobs running in their environment, but our postmortems need a clear operational attribution before we accept the proposed SLA carveout in the contract.

Can Redwood confirm what evidence you can provide to support an ops responsibility split (e.g., packet-level traces, KV-cache hit rates, GPU utilization slices, and timestamps mapped to request IDs)? Also - what format would you prefer for us to supply our firewall and peering logs?

I've attached a short network trace from 2028-07-19 showing a representative window.

Attachments: network-trace-20280719.log (text)

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Halcyon Therapeutics

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@halcyon-tx.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@halcyon-tx.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes in private VPC — need attribution

Priya — thanks for the sample trace and the clear ask. We can produce the following evidence bundle that customers typically accept for a shared-responsibility SLA appendix: 

- Per-request timing logs correlated to Redwood request IDs (t0 request arrival, t1 routing, t2 kernel start, t3 token emit).
- GPU utilization heatmaps and per-process snapshots for the timeframe.
- KV-cache hit/miss stats and prefix cache correlation.
- Packet captures / pcap slices (we will redact customer payloads as required).

To make this practical and audit-ready, I'd propose an "ops playbook" in the SLA appendix that defines: evidence types, retention windows, a canonical timeline format, and a small set of attribution rules (e.g., if egress latency > X ms and upstream firewall shows queued packets, attribute to customer).

If that sounds reasonable, we can draft a short SLO amendment and a companion runbook. Vanessa, Marcus — can you weigh in on what artifacts we can produce from the private VPC agent and any redaction constraints?

Karthik
Director, Product (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@halcyon-tx.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes in private VPC — need attribution

+1 to Karthik's proposal. A couple of practical constraints and asks from our side: 

- The private control-plane agent can emit per-request markers and aggregated performance logs; however, full packet captures must be customer-provided due to privacy/firewall ownership. We'll accept pcap slices from Halcyon and correlate timestamps with our markers.
- For contractual language, we suggest a three-tier attribution model in the appendix: 
  1) Redwood-owned: clear runtime or infra service failure (kernel crash, disk OOM, Redwood-managed control-plane outage).
  2) Joint/indeterminate: transient network handoffs where both sides show sub-threshold errors — requires a joint postmortem.
  3) Customer-owned: evidence of edge queuing, NAT timeouts, or 3rd-party network provider issues reflected in customer routing logs.

- We'll publish a redacted example timeline (slo-draft-v1.pdf) and a template timeline CSV that maps request IDs to markers for handoff during audits.

Marcus — Jordan, please add the minimal set of fields we need in the timeline CSV. Priya / Samir, if you can share your firewall logs (s3 link or Drive link), we'll map them into the timeline.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@halcyon-tx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes in private VPC — need attribution

I've attached the SLO draft and an example CSV layout. Key fields we will populate from Redwood side: request_id, arrival_ts, routing_ts, kernel_start_ts, token_emit_ts, kv_cache_hit, gpu_util_pct. From the customer side we need: firewall_ingress_ts, firewall_egress_ts, peering_latency_ms, upstream_provider_tag.

Attachment: slo-draft-v1.pdf (pdf)

Sample excerpt from the csv (tabular view pasted inline):
request_id	arrival_ts	routing_ts	kernel_start_ts	token_emit_ts	kv_cache_hit	gpu_util_pct
r-00123	2028-07-19T14:08:02.342Z	2028-07-19T14:08:02.360Z	2028-07-19T14:08:02.412Z	2028-07-19T14:08:02.490Z	true	78

Notes: the tight windows above demonstrate that when kernel_start -> token_emit expands beyond typical threshold (~200ms for this model under current load), we look first at prefix cache miss rates and oversized batch formation. If the customer's firewall shows queued timestamps overlapping the window, we mark as customer-owned latency.

Jordan — can you add a short checklist for "must-provide" artifacts from the customer for our security team to approve redaction?

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@halcyon-tx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@halcyon-tx.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes in private VPC — need attribution

Thanks all — that approach looks sensible and actionable. We will: 

1) Share two weeks of firewall/peering logs to the Drive link you provided (we'll redact customer payloads and provide accompanying manifest).
2) Export our NAT/edge queueing timestamps for the sample windows you have highlighted.
3) Accept a short SLA appendix with the three-tier attribution model; legal will take the draft but PMs want the operational playbook finalized first.

Next steps agreed: Redwood to produce the timeline template + example (Marcus), Halcyon to drop logs to Drive by end of next week, then a joint 60-minute replay session to annotate the timeline. If that reveals a systemic Redwood runtime regression, we will request a credit/roll-forward under HD-4932.

Priya Rao
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Halcyon Therapeutics
